JAMM 275 –FALL 2017 Homework Assignments 25 points each Homework #1 Camera Checkout Paper: Due Tuesday, Sept.19 at the beginning of class as a paper hard copy (late and/or emailed papers will not be accepted.) Familiarize yourself with cameras and available gear in the JAMM Equipment Checkout Facilities. This assignment stipulates that you (individually, not with a partner or group) must responsibly reserve, obtain and return a camera and equipment from JAMM (not from a friend, not your own personal camera, not a camera from ITS Media Center). Check out a camera from the JAMM facility and experiment with it referencing your assigned reading. Write a one-page paper that addresses the following: When did you make the request for an equipment reservation? How did you find out if the gear was available for the day you requested? What days/dates did you check the equipment out? What gear did you reserve and why? What questions did you ask the person who checked the gear out to you? Was the employee able to help you and answer all of your questions? What equipment tests did you conduct before you left the RTV when checking out? What experiments did you conduct based on your reading and why? What challenges or obstacles did you encounter with this production assignment? What did you learn about production based on your experiments? What did you learn about scheduling for production? What did you do to insure that equipment was not stolen, lost or damaged? What questions did the JAMM employee ask you when you returned the gear? What questions do you have about reserving and using JAMM’s gear in the future? Homework #2 Camera Experiments: Due Thursday, Oct.19 by 3:00 p.m Responsibly reserve, acquire and return a camera and a mounting device (tripod, monopod, fig-rig, etc.) from the JAMM equipment checkout facilities. This assignment stipulates that you (individually, not with a partner or group) must obtain and return a camera with at least one mounting device from JAMM (not from a friend, not your own personal camera, not a camera from ITS Media Center, not from your job, etc.) Experiment with different camera placements, heights, angles, movements, shot sizes and compositions. Produce, shoot and edit a 30 second clip that is a good representation of your camera exploration… for example, show a first attempt and then a corrected/revised attempt that demonstrates your improvement over time with a variety of shots, moves, etc… and that also demonstrates your understanding of the textbook. Upload that clip to your ShortsU account and to your personal YouTube or Vimeo account and email deniseb@uidaho.edu those links to the complete experiment by 3:00 p.m. on October 19th. (Please note video host websites don’t automatically make your content available for public viewing after your upload is complete. The content must be public by the deadline so plan accordingly). Along with the link to your finished video answer the following questions and include them in the body of the email. Make sure to include your first and last name in the email so you get credit for the assignment. The subject line of the email should be: First Name & Last Name, Camera Experiments, JAMM 275. What gear did you use and why? What troubleshooting did you do during preproduction to make sure that you could actually complete the assignment? Can you describe your experiment and what you were trying to accomplish with it? How do your experiments relate to your reading? Do you think you were successful executing your experiments, why or why not? What did you learn about composition from this assignment? What specific shot sizes did you attempt and why? What did you learn about camera height from this assignment? What did you learn about camera angle from this assignment? What did you learn about camera and subject movement from this assignment? How did you manually control the camera (be specific)? Do you feel more confident operating cameras, why or why not? What will you do differently in the future based on what you learned from your experiments.

Homework #3 Music Video Script: Due Tuesday, Nov.14 at the beginning of class as a paper hard copy (late and/or emailed scripts will not be accepted.) Create a two-column script for a Music Video that dictates all audio and video, is no less than 30 seconds in length and no longer than 5 minutes. On the right next to the audio column include a third column that indicates the exact timings, accounting for every beat and rhythm in the song and every frame of video you need to capture in order to realize your vision. You may not alter another artist’s work (i.e. cutting off a song half way through or adding additional sound to the mix with the song). You may not use music that is a theme song for a television show or web series. You may not chose music from a motion picture soundtrack or motion picture score. You must select a “pop song”, no instrumentals! You will not be allowed to change songs once the script has been submitted so make wise choices and be sure you can get an AIFF/MP3/WAV version of the song. The script must be typed. Put the video on the left and the audio on the right and indicate the exact timings of shots/sequences on a third column. (See chapter 17 for examples of formatting). In the top left corner of the script include the following: Your Name, Artist Name, Title of Song, Album, TRT of Song, Genre: Performance, Narrative, Non-narrative, some combination of 2 or all 3, and Style: Realism, Formalism or Classicism * If you do not submit a script you will be assigned to produce a song to produce a video for. FORMAT SAMPLE VIDEO AUDIO (TIME) Slow fade up to XLS of empty country Slow guitar intro building 0-:07 road in black and white, a young girl appears (Key over titles) XCU of the young girl’s face in color Big drum beat and up-tempo begins :07-:09 as she screams and then falls out of frame MLS of the young girl falling in slow-mo Bass beats, Lyrics begin :09-:14… Jump cutting to the beat as she changes positions “You sit there in your…here he comes.” Homework #4 Editing & Software Exploration: Due Thursday, Nov. 30 by 3:00 p.m. Demonstrate your ability to use keyboard short cuts and to control the software interface in Final Cut Pro as well as experiment with editing theories, techniques and aesthetics. Reserve time to edit in the JAMM Production Facilities. Manage your media workflow with labeled libraries, events, and projects routing your media to the appropriate hard-drive or external drive. Try out different editing theories (parallel cutting, complexity editing, montage, match cutting, etc). Experiment with effects, filters, motion controls, titles, and so forth on any footage you have shot. Create a 30 second clip that is a good representation of your experiments and demonstrates you ability to use Final Cut Pro. Upload that clip to your ShortsU account and to your personal YouTube or Vimeo account and email deniseb@uidaho.edu those links to the complete experiment by 3:00 p.m. on November 30th. (Please note video host websites don’t automatically make your content available for public viewing after your upload is complete. The content must be public by the deadline so plan accordingly). Along with the link to your finished video answer the following questions and include them in the body of the email. Make sure to include your first and last name in the email so you get credit for the assignment. The subject line of the email should be: First Name & Last Name, Editing Experiments, JAMM 275. What NLE did you use and what dates/times did you reserve it? How long did you spend experimenting with editing? What are the keyboard shortcuts for setting in-points and out-points? What does setting in/out- points do to footage? What is the keyboard short cut for the range selection tool? How is the range selection tool used and why is it used? What is the keyboard short cut or FCP button that allows you to insert a clip between two clips on the timeline? Why is this insert function important and how does it save time in editing? How do you access the inspector in FCP and what does the inspector allow you to control? How do you add a transition and how do you change the duration of the transition? How do you add an effect and how can you control the effect? How do you add a title and how can you manipulate titles? How do you change the speed of a clip? How do you export a finished project? What editing theories did you practice with and why? Did you run into any technical difficulty and if so how did you resolve it? What did you learn about editing? What will you do differently in the future to improve your editing?
